questions.prompt: Identify one software type that could be used to create a visualisation diagram.
questions.markSchemeHint: Accept Desktop Publishing (DTP), graphics/image editing software, presentation software, drawing software, or word processing software.

questions.prompt: Link each user interaction method to the appropriate advantage. (You will only use two interaction methods to match the two advantages.)
matchingLeft: Beneficial to those who use assistive technology
Reduces the chances of selecting an incorrect option
questions.markSchemeHint: Voice -> Beneficial to those who use assistive technology (1 mark); Mouse -> Reduces the chances of selecting an incorrect option (1 mark).

questions.scenarioContext: You have collected information from a client.
questions.prompt: What is meant by the term information?
questions.markSchemeHint: Data that has been processed / given context, structure, and meaning so it can be understood (1 mark per valid point up to 2).

questions.prompt:
Identify the data type shown below that could be used in a database design.

[ Yes/No ]
questions.markSchemeHint: Boolean.

questions.prompt: Which of these is not a limited choice data validation tool?
questions.markSchemeHint: B) Input mask (1 mark).

questions.scenarioContext: A project manager needs to take electronic files to a meeting with a client.
questions.prompt: What physical storage device could the project manager use to take these electronic files to the meeting?
questions.markSchemeHint: Accept USB flash drive / memory stick, external hard drive / SSD, SD card / memory card, or optical disc (CD/DVD).

questions.scenarioContext: A hacker has maliciously stolen data from you.
questions.prompt: What type of 'hat' hacking is this?
questions.markSchemeHint: Black hat (hacking).

questions.prompt: Describe what is meant by the term ransomware.
questions.markSchemeHint: Malware that encrypts/locks a user's files or device (1) and demands a payment/ransom to restore access or decrypt the data (1).

questions.prompt: Which logical prevention measure converts data into code to prevent unauthorised access?
questions.markSchemeHint: Encryption.

questions.prompt: Identify the legislation that relates to the misuse of personal data.
questions.markSchemeHint: Data Protection Act (2018) / UK GDPR.

questions.scenarioContext: Gender is one audience demographic.
questions.prompt: Identify two other audience demographics.
questions.markSchemeHint: Accept any two of: Age, Location, Accessibility / disability, Income / socio-economic group, Education, Ethnicity/culture, Lifestyle/interests.

questions.scenarioContext:
Progress Fitness Centre (PFC) is a fitness and health centre. Amir is designing a mobile app to allow customers of PFC to:
• book fitness classes
• pay for membership
• read customer reviews.

Amir uses a wireframe for the design of the mobile app.
questions.prompt:
Create a wireframe to plan the content of the home screen for the mobile app for PFC.
Marks will be awarded for: Content and Layout.
questions.markSchemeHint: Up to 4 marks for Content (PFC title/logo, navigation/buttons for Book Classes, Pay Membership, Customer Reviews, login/account, placeholders for images/text, annotations) and up to 4 marks for Layout (mobile screen portrait frame, logical hierarchy, clean wireframe conventions without final colours/images, well-proportioned spacing).

questions.scenarioContext: Amir is creating a wireframe for the Progress Fitness Centre mobile app.
questions.prompt: Identify one type of software that could be used to create a wireframe for the design of a mobile app.
questions.markSchemeHint: Dedicated wireframing/prototyping software, DTP software, presentation software, graphics/vector drawing software, or word processing software.

questions.scenarioContext: Follow-up to Q12(b)(i).
questions.prompt: Justify your choice of software.
questions.markSchemeHint: 1 mark for a valid feature of the chosen software + 1 mark for explaining how it helps Amir design the wireframe (e.g., built-in UI templates/shapes, easy to drag/rearrange elements, easy to share/edit digitally).

questions.scenarioContext: Progress Fitness Centre (PFC) mobile app design.
questions.prompt: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage of a wireframe being used to show the design of a mobile app.
questions.markSchemeHint: Advantage (1+1): shows structure/layout clearly before coding, easy/cheap to amend early based on client feedback. Disadvantage (1+1): lacks visual styling/colours/branding so client may struggle to visualise the final app, or does not show full interactive functionality.

questions.scenarioContext: Progress Fitness Centre (PFC) mobile app has been created. Testing will be carried out before the mobile app is launched.
questions.prompt: Explain one reason why testing would be carried out on the mobile app.
questions.markSchemeHint: 1 mark for reason (e.g., find and fix errors/bugs, check it meets user/client requirements, ensure usability/compatibility) + 1 mark for impact on PFC/customers before launch.

questions.scenarioContext: Testing the Progress Fitness Centre mobile app before launch.
questions.prompt: Identify two different types of user tests that could be carried out on the mobile app.
questions.markSchemeHint: Accept any two OCR user testing types: usability testing, accessibility testing, compatibility testing, alpha testing, beta testing, acceptance testing, functionality/navigation testing.

questions.scenarioContext: To access and use the mobile app customers will be required to enter their personal details. PFC will need to comply with data protection legislation.
questions.prompt: Identify and describe one action PFC will need to take in order to comply with data protection legislation.
questions.markSchemeHint: Action (1) + Description (1): e.g., keep data secure (using encryption/passwords), gain customer consent (explain how data is used), keep data accurate/up-to-date, do not keep data longer than necessary, only collect data needed for membership/bookings.

questions.scenarioContext: Customers will be able to access the mobile app using a smartphone.
questions.prompt: Identify one characteristic of a smartphone that makes this device appropriate to access the mobile app.
questions.markSchemeHint: Portable/lightweight, touchscreen interface, built-in Wi-Fi/mobile data (4G/5G), battery powered, supports mobile apps/notifications.

questions.scenarioContext: Customers using the PFC app on their smartphone.
questions.prompt: Identify one physical security measure that could be used by customers using an app on their smartphone. Justify your answer.
questions.markSchemeHint: Measure (1): e.g., Biometrics (fingerprint/face recognition), locking device away/keeping device secure, privacy screen filter. Justification (2): explains how it prevents unauthorised people accessing the smartphone/app and protects customer personal/payment data.

questions.scenarioContext: Progress Fitness Centre (PFC) customers can access the Wi-Fi in the centre to make bookings for classes.
questions.prompt: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage to the customers of using the Wi-Fi.
questions.markSchemeHint: Advantage (1+1): saves personal mobile data allowance / free to use / faster or more reliable indoor signal. Disadvantage (1+1): security risk on public/shared Wi-Fi (interception/man-in-the-middle), slow bandwidth when many members connect, limited range inside the building.

questions.scenarioContext: Progress Fitness Centre (PFC) will use social media to promote the Centre and attract new customers.
questions.prompt: Identify and explain one advantage and one disadvantage to PFC of using social media for this purpose.
questions.markSchemeHint: Advantage + explanation (2): low cost/free marketing, wide reach/shareable posts, targeted local advertising, instant two-way customer engagement. Disadvantage + explanation (2): public negative reviews/trolling can harm reputation, requires ongoing staff time to manage/update, excludes people who do not use social media.

questions.scenarioContext: PFC wants to show some of the exercise classes on their social media page.
questions.prompt: State one digital communication method that could be used to show the exercise classes on their social media page.
questions.markSchemeHint: Accept video / vlog / livestream, image / photograph / infographic, or animation.

questions.scenarioContext: Follow-up to Q14(b)(i).
questions.prompt: Justify your chosen method.
questions.markSchemeHint: 1 mark for valid reason + 1 mark for contextual link to showing exercise classes on social media (e.g., video shows movement/atmosphere in real time so potential members see what classes are like and feel encouraged to join).

questions.scenarioContext: Progress Fitness Centre (PFC). The music for the exercise classes is accessed through a smart device connected to the Internet of Everything (IoE).
questions.prompt: Identify the two pillars of the IoE that are used when accessing the music.
questions.markSchemeHint: Accept two of the relevant four IoE pillars: People, Process, Data, Things (specifically Things/Device + Data or People + Process depending on context).

questions.scenarioContext: The music for exercise classes at PFC is accessed through a smart device connected to the IoE.
questions.prompt: Explain, using an example, how the smart device can be tailored to meet the needs of the different class instructors.
questions.markSchemeHint: Up to 4 marks: explains customisation/personalisation (e.g., individual instructor profiles/playlists, voice commands, scheduled volume/tempo presets, linking to lighting/timers) with a clear example linked to different classes (e.g., calm playlist for yoga vs upbeat playlist for spin class) and benefit to instructors.

questions.scenarioContext: Tailoring the smart device at PFC to meet the needs of different class instructors.
questions.prompt: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage of tailoring the smart device to meet the needs of the different class instructors.
questions.markSchemeHint: Advantage (1+1): saves setup time between classes / improves class experience with suitable playlists/settings. Disadvantage (1+1): requires staff training/time to configure profiles, relies on Wi-Fi/internet connectivity, or privacy/security concerns if voice profiles/data are stored.

questions.scenarioContext: Progress Fitness Centre (PFC) is a fitness and health centre. Amir is designing a mobile app to allow customers of PFC to book fitness classes, pay for membership, and read customer reviews. As the number of customers using the mobile app has increased, PFC is considering different data storage solutions.
questions.prompt:
Discuss the use of a cloud-based storage solution and a physical storage solution for storing and accessing the data downloaded from the mobile app.

In your answer you must consider:
• advantages and disadvantages of a cloud-based storage solution
• advantages and disadvantages of a physical storage solution.
questions.markSchemeHint: OCR 9-mark Level of Response (Level 1: 1–3, Level 2: 4–6, Level 3: 7–9). Must give balanced discussion of both cloud (scalability for growing customer numbers, remote access, automatic backups vs ongoing subscription cost, internet dependency, third-party security) and physical storage (full local control, one-off hardware cost, offline access vs limited capacity/upgrade cost, physical damage/theft risk, manual backups) applied to PFC, with a reasoned conclusion.
